name: Cefuroxime
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Cefuroxime is excreted unchanged by the kidneys (about 89% of an IV dose in 8 hours). Oral cefuroxime axetil keeps the standard dose but lengthens the interval when creatinine clearance (CrCl) is below 30 mL/min; IV cefuroxime is reduced to 750 mg every 12 hours at CrCl 10–20 and every 24 hours below 10. Both labels give an extra dose at the end of each hemodialysis.
kidney_function_basis: Labels use CrCl (mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault). Oral: adjust below 30. IV: adjust at 20 or less.

bands.recommendation: Oral and IV: usual dose (oral: no adjustment at CrCl 30 or more; IV: usual dose above 20) (labels).
Oral: CrCl 10 to <30, standard dose every 24 hours. IV: CrCl 21–29, usual 750 mg to 1.5 g every 8 hours; CrCl 10–20, 750 mg every 12 hours (labels).
Oral: CrCl 10–14, standard dose every 24 hours; below 10 (not on HD), every 48 hours. IV: CrCl 10–14, 750 mg every 12 hours; below 10, 750 mg every 24 hours (labels).

hd: Oral: one extra standard dose at the end of each dialysis. IV: a further dose at the end of dialysis, as cefuroxime is dialyzable (labels).
pd: No peritoneal dialysis dosing in the labels (serum levels can be reduced by PD, overdose sections). ISPD 2022 gives no intraperitoneal cefuroxime dose. Specialist input.
crrt: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
dialyzable: Yes: hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis reduce serum levels (labels). About 50% protein bound.
monitoring: CrCl for dose; seizures or encephalopathy with overdose in kidney impairment (label overdose section); diarrhea (CDAD).

pediatric.approved_ages: Oral tablets: children who can swallow tablets whole (3 months to 12 years for maxillary sinusitis). IV: over 3 months (labels).
pediatric.usual_dose: Oral tablets under 13 years: 250 mg every 12 hours (otitis media, sinusitis). IV over 3 months: 50 to 100 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours; bone and joint 150 mg/kg/day every 8 hours; meningitis 200 to 240 mg/kg/day every 6 to 8 hours (labels).
pediatric.max_dose: Not above the maximum adult dose (IV label).

renal.recommendation: Usual dose; adult changes start below CrCl 30 (oral) or at 20 (IV) (labels).
IV: modify dosing frequency consistent with the adult table (IV label). Oral pediatric: not stated.
IV: modify dosing frequency consistent with the adult table (IV label). Oral pediatric: not stated.

pediatric.hd: IV: frequency consistent with adult recommendations, including the dose after dialysis (IV label). Specialist input.
pediatric.crrt: No pediatric CRRT data in the cited sources. Specialist input.

adult: Oral tablets and suspension are not bioequivalent (label); the kidney table applies to both by interval change.

label_note: The pinned US label is oral cefuroxime axetil tablets; about half of PH products (387 of 793) are injections. IV kidney dosing here is from the B. Braun DUPLEX IV label (NDA050780, version December 5, 2020), cached in the repo's label history. Consider adding it as an alternate label in tools/drugdb/label_overrides.json.
